title: 1 Thessalonians 5 — The day of the Lord like a thief in the night + closing exhortations

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT), ed. Michael W. Holmes (Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software, 2010), printed text with the variant-marker sigla removed. Principal witnesses for 1 Thessalonians: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01), Codex Vaticanus (B/03), Codex Alexandrinus (A/02), Codex Claromontanus (D/06); the papyri P30 and P46 preserve fragments of the letter. Variants against NA28 and the Byzantine and Textus Receptus readings are reported in the verse commentary (overlay convention sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians).

founderDecisionRecommendations.1TH-5:3 'Peace and security': Confirm. RSV/NRSV/ESV rendering; pax et securitas background (Koester; Weima) is an independent scholarly ground; reception note states the agreement with the canon as an agreement and notes the Greek does not oppose the two terms.
founderDecisionRecommendations.1TH-5:12 'to respect': Confirm. BDAG cites this verse for the sense; RSV/NRSV/ESV; literal 'know' kept in note.
founderDecisionRecommendations.adelphoi 'brothers': Confirm. Formal equivalent (ESV), corpus precedent (Matt 23:8; Rev 6:11); inclusive sense given once at 5:1. Optionally trim the house-style clause from the overlay rationale.
founderDecisionRecommendations.No reception note at 1 Thess 5:23: Confirm. No canon book cites 5:23; LWTE-4:88's statement on the soul cites no Pauline text. Attaching it would put a WoH reading into the apparatus without a citation basis.

paragraphs.text: Περὶ δὲ τῶν χρόνων καὶ τῶν καιρῶν, ἀδελφοί, οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε ὑμῖν γράφεσθαι,
paragraphs.translit: peri de tōn chronōn kai tōn kairōn, adelphoi, ou chreian echete hymin graphesthai,

i18n.en: Now concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need that anything be written to you.

notes.official:
*Peri de tōn chronōn kai tōn kairōn* 'Now concerning the times and the seasons': *peri de* introduces a new topic, as at 4:9 (cf. 4:13 *peri tōn koimōmenōn*). The pair *chronoi kai kairoi* is a fixed expression (Acts 1:7; Dan 2:21 LXX; Wis 8:8), here the timing of the day of the Lord. *ou chreian echete hymin graphesthai* 'you have no need that anything be written to you' (ASV 'that aught be written'): Paul declines to write about what he says they already know, as at 4:9. *adelphoi* 'brothers' (`adelphoi-brothers-rendering-1-thessalonians`); the plural address includes the women of the assembly (BDAG s.v. *adelphos* 2a; cf. Acts 17:4).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 4) cites 1 Thess 5:1-3 for the words 'peace' and 'security'; the citation and the canon's reading are given at 5:3.

paragraphs.text: αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκριβῶς οἴδατε ὅτι ἡμέρα κυρίου ὡς κλέπτης ἐν νυκτὶ οὕτως ἔρχεται.
paragraphs.translit: autoi gar akribōs oidate hoti hēmera kyriou hōs kleptēs en nykti houtōs erchetai.

i18n.en: For you yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night.

notes.official:
*hēmera kyriou* 'the day of the Lord': the Septuagint's form of *yôm YHWH* (Amos 5:18-20; Joel 2:1, 11; Zeph 1:14-16), the day on which God intervenes in judgment. *kyrios* is 'Lord' (`theos-kyrios-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-1-thessalonians`); the Hebrew-text entries that transliterate YHWH are not applied, because the Greek does not carry the name. The phrase has no article in the SBLGNT, as a fixed expression that is definite in sense; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have *hē* (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`). *hōs kleptēs en nykti* 'like a thief in the night' takes up a saying of Jesus (Matt 24:43; Luke 12:39), echoed at 2 Pet 3:10 and Rev 3:3; 16:15. *akribōs oidate* 'you know perfectly' (ASV), that is, accurately; *erchetai* 'comes', a present for a certain future. The central `as-saa-the-hour-quranic-eschatology-cross-corpus-yom-yhwh-parousia` and `iqtaraba-eschatological-reckoning-draws-near-quranic-hebrew-bible-nt-cross-corpus` name this passage as background to the Qur'anic 'Hour'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** Part of the passage 5:1-3 cited in *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 4); see 5:3.

paragraphs.text: ὅταν λέγωσιν· Εἰρήνη καὶ ἀσφάλεια, τότε αἰφνίδιος αὐτοῖς ἐφίσταται ὄλεθρος ὥσπερ ἡ ὠδὶν τῇ ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐκφύγωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hotan legōsin· eirēnē kai asphaleia, tote aiphnidios autois ephistatai olethros hōsper hē ōdin tē en gastri echousē, kai ou mē ekphygōsin.

i18n.en: When they are saying, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction comes upon them, as birth pangs come upon a woman with child, and they will by no means escape.

notes.official:
*Eirēnē kai asphaleia* 'Peace and security': *asphaleia* is 'safety, security' (BDAG s.v. *asphaleia*). The line follows the RSV, NRSV and ESV rather than the ASV and KJV 'Peace and safety' (`eirene-kai-asphaleia-peace-and-security-1-thess-5-3`). Many commentators hear in the pair the Roman imperial theme *pax et securitas* and take 'they' to be those who trust in it (H. Koester, 'Imperial Ideology and Paul's Eschatology in 1 Thessalonians', in R. A. Horsley, ed., *Paul and Empire*, 1997; J. A. D. Weima, *1-2 Thessalonians*, BECNT, 2014, ad loc.); others read an echo of the false prophets' 'Peace, peace, when there is no peace' (Jer 6:14; 8:11; Ezek 13:10). 'security' suits either reading.

*aiphnidios ... olethros* 'sudden destruction'. *hōsper hē ōdin tē en gastri echousē* 'as birth pangs come upon a woman with child' (ASV 'travail'; cf. Isa 13:6-8; Jer 6:24): sudden, and unavoidable once begun. *ou mē ekphygōsin* 'they will by no means escape', with the emphatic double negative. Text: the SBLGNT has no connective; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus add *gar* (KJV 'For when they shall say') (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 4), listing the solutions the messages propose, among them the abolition of military service: « l'abolition du service militaire et la mise au service de la paix des militaires de carrière: on ne peut continuer à rechercher en même temps la «paix» et la «sécurité» comme nous y invitait Paul de Tarse (I, Thess., V, 1à 3) » (English edition: 'the abolition of military service and the placing of career soldiers at the service of world peace: we cannot continue to search for “peace and security” at the same time, as Paul of Tarsus said in Chapter 5 of his first Epistle to the Thessalonians.'). The canon quotes only the two nouns and reads them as two aims that cannot be pursued together: peace, and military security. The line's 'Peace and security' agrees with the canon's wording, but the choice rests on the lexicon and the background given above. In the Greek, 'Peace and security' is what 'they' say before sudden destruction comes; the verse does not itself set peace against security.

paragraphs.text: ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σκότει, ἵνα ἡ ἡμέρα ὑμᾶς ὡς κλέπτης καταλάβῃ,
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de, adelphoi, ouk este en skotei, hina hē hēmera hymas hōs kleptēs katalabē,

i18n.en: But you, brothers, are not in darkness, that the day should overtake you like a thief;

notes.official: *hymeis de, adelphoi, ouk este en skotei* 'But you, brothers, are not in darkness': the contrast of light and darkness governs vv 4-8. *hina hē hēmera hymas hōs kleptēs katalabē* 'that the day should overtake you like a thief'. Text: Westcott-Hort print *kleptas* 'like thieves', the reading of Alexandrinus and Vaticanus (Metzger, *Textual Commentary*, ad loc.), which turns the image: the day surprises them as daylight surprises thieves. The SBLGNT, NA28, Tregelles and the Byzantine text read *kleptēs* (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).

paragraphs.text: πάντες γὰρ ὑμεῖς υἱοὶ φωτός ἐστε καὶ υἱοὶ ἡμέρας. οὐκ ἐσμὲν νυκτὸς οὐδὲ σκότους·
paragraphs.translit: pantes gar hymeis huioi phōtos este kai huioi hēmeras. ouk esmen nyktos oude skotous·

i18n.en: for you are all sons of light and sons of the day. We are not of the night nor of darkness.

notes.official: *huioi phōtos ... huioi hēmeras* 'sons of light and sons of the day': a Semitic idiom in which 'son of X' means one marked by X (cf. Luke 16:8; John 12:36; Eph 5:8; the 'sons of light' and 'sons of darkness' of the Qumran Community Rule, 1QS 1:9-10, and the War Scroll). The literal form is kept (ASV); KJV and NRSV 'children'. Paul moves from 'you' to 'we' in the second sentence. Text: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus lack *gar* 'for' (KJV 'Ye are all') (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).

paragraphs.text: ἄρα οὖν μὴ καθεύδωμεν ὡς οἱ λοιποί, ἀλλὰ γρηγορῶμεν καὶ νήφωμεν.
paragraphs.translit: ara oun mē katheudōmen hōs hoi loipoi, alla grēgorōmen kai nēphōmen.

i18n.en: So then let us not sleep, as the rest do, but let us watch and be sober.

notes.official: *ara oun* 'so then'. *mē katheudōmen ... alla grēgorōmen kai nēphōmen* 'let us not sleep ... but let us watch and be sober': *grēgoreō* is 'stay awake' and 'be watchful' (BDAG s.v. 1, 2); 'watch' (ASV, KJV) keeps both senses (RSV, NRSV 'keep awake'; cf. Rev 16:15 'the one who stays awake'). Sleep here is moral inattention; at v 10 the same two verbs take a different sense. *hōs hoi loipoi* 'as the rest do' (cf. 4:13 'the rest, who have no hope'). Text: the Byzantine text adds *kai* ('as the rest also do') (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).

paragraphs.text: οἱ γὰρ καθεύδοντες νυκτὸς καθεύδουσιν, καὶ οἱ μεθυσκόμενοι νυκτὸς μεθύουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: hoi gar katheudontes nyktos katheudousin, kai hoi methyskomenoi nyktos methyousin·

i18n.en: For those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk, are drunk at night.

notes.official: A proverbial observation: sleep and drunkenness belong to the night. *methyskomenoi* 'those who get drunk' and *methyousin* 'are drunk' distinguish becoming drunk from being drunk.

paragraphs.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἡμέρας ὄντες νήφωμεν, ἐνδυσάμενοι θώρακα πίστεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ περικεφαλαίαν ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας·
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis de hēmeras ontes nēphōmen, endysamenoi thōraka pisteōs kai agapēs kai perikephalaian elpida sōtērias·

i18n.en: But since we are of the day, let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation.

notes.official: *hēmeras ontes* 'since we are of the day'. *endysamenoi thōraka pisteōs kai agapēs kai perikephalaian elpida sōtērias* 'having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation': from God's armour in Isa 59:17 ('righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation upon his head'), transferred to the believers and arranged by the triad faith, love and hope (1:3; cf. Wis 5:17-18; Eph 6:14-17).

paragraphs.text: ὅτι οὐκ ἔθετο ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς εἰς ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ εἰς περιποίησιν σωτηρίας διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: hoti ouk etheto hēmas ho theos eis orgēn alla eis peripoiēsin sōtērias dia tou kyriou hēmōn iēsou christou,

i18n.en: For God did not appoint us to wrath, but to the obtaining of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,

notes.official: *ouk etheto hēmas ho theos eis orgēn* 'God did not appoint us to wrath' ('God' per `theos-kyrios-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-1-thessalonians`); *orgē* is 'the wrath to come' of 1:10. *eis peripoiēsin sōtērias* 'to the obtaining of salvation' (ASV): *peripoiēsis* is 'gaining possession, acquiring' (BDAG). 'our Lord Jesus Christ': 'Jesus' and 'Christ' per the central `iēsous-yehoshua-yhwh-saves-folk-etymology-cross-corpus` and `christos-māšîaḥ-anointed-one-cross-corpus-greek-hebrew-aramaic`.

paragraphs.text: τοῦ ἀποθανόντος περὶ ἡμῶν ἵνα εἴτε γρηγορῶμεν εἴτε καθεύδωμεν ἅμα σὺν αὐτῷ ζήσωμεν.
paragraphs.translit: tou apothanontos peri hēmōn hina eite grēgorōmen eite katheudōmen hama syn autō zēsōmen.

i18n.en: who died for us, so that whether we wake or sleep we may live together with him.

notes.official: *tou apothanontos peri hēmōn* 'who died for us'. Text: the SBLGNT prints *peri* with Westcott-Hort and Tregelles, and here departs from NA28, which with the Byzantine text reads *hyper*; both mean 'for, on behalf of' here (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`). *eite grēgorōmen eite katheudōmen* 'whether we wake or sleep': the verbs of v 6 are now used, on the usual reading, for 'whether we are alive or dead' (cf. 4:13-17, where the dead are 'those who sleep', with *koimaomai*). The line keeps the image, as the ASV does (BDAG s.v. *katheudō*; A. J. Malherbe, *The Letters to the Thessalonians*, AB 32B, 2000, ad loc.). *hama syn autō zēsōmen* 'we may live together with him' (cf. 4:17).

paragraphs.text: διὸ παρακαλεῖτε ἀλλήλους καὶ οἰκοδομεῖτε εἷς τὸν ἕνα, καθὼς καὶ ποιεῖτε.
paragraphs.translit: dio parakaleite allēlous kai oikodomeite heis ton hena, kathōs kai poieite.

i18n.en: Therefore exhort one another and build one another up, just as you are also doing.

notes.official: *dio parakaleite allēlous* 'Therefore exhort one another': the same verb closes the preceding section at 4:18 ('comfort one another with these words') and covers 'exhort', 'encourage' and 'comfort' (BDAG s.v. *parakaleō*). 'exhort' (ASV) is kept here and at v 14, where 'encourage' renders the distinct verb *paramytheomai*. *oikodomeite heis ton hena* 'build one another up' (literally 'one the one').

paragraphs.text: Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, εἰδέναι τοὺς κοπιῶντας ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ προϊσταμένους ὑμῶν ἐν κυρίῳ καὶ νουθετοῦντας ὑμᾶς,
paragraphs.translit: erōtōmen de hymas, adelphoi, eidenai tous kopiōntas en hymin kai proistamenous hymōn en kyriō kai nouthetountas hymas,

i18n.en: But we ask you, brothers, to respect those who labor among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you,

notes.official: *eidenai tous kopiōntas en hymin* 'to respect those who labor among you': *oida* here means 'recognize the worth of, respect' (BDAG s.v. *oida*, citing this verse; RSV, NRSV 'respect'), not 'be acquainted with'. The ASV and KJV 'to know' is literal but hides the sense (`eidenai-respect-1-thess-5-12`). *proistamenous hymōn en kyriō* 'are over you in the Lord' (ASV, RSV): *proistēmi* is 'be at the head of, lead' and also 'care for' (BDAG); NRSV 'have charge of you'. The three participles share one article and describe one group. *erōtōmen* 'we ask' (ASV 'beseech'). 'Lord' per `theos-kyrios-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-1-thessalonians`; 'brothers' per `adelphoi-brothers-rendering-1-thessalonians`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἡγεῖσθαι αὐτοὺς ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ διὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτῶν. εἰρηνεύετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai hēgeisthai autous hyperekperissou en agapē dia to ergon autōn. eirēneuete en heautois.

i18n.en: and to esteem them very highly in love because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves.

notes.official: *hēgeisthai autous hyperekperissou en agapē* 'to esteem them very highly in love': the rare double compound *hyperekperissou* (3:10; Eph 3:20) means 'beyond all measure'. *dia to ergon autōn* 'because of their work'. *eirēneuete en heautois* 'Be at peace among yourselves'. Text: Tregelles prints *en autois* 'with them', that is, with the leaders of v 12, a reading found in part of the manuscript tradition; the SBLGNT, NA28, Westcott-Hort and the Byzantine text read *heautois*. Tregelles also prints the adverb *hyperekperissōs*, with the same sense (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).

paragraphs.text: παρακαλοῦμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, νουθετεῖτε τοὺς ἀτάκτους, παραμυθεῖσθε τοὺς ὀλιγοψύχους, ἀντέχεσθε τῶν ἀσθενῶν, μακροθυμεῖτε πρὸς πάντας.
paragraphs.translit: parakaloumen de hymas, adelphoi, noutheteite tous ataktous, paramytheisthe tous oligopsychous, antechesthe tōn asthenōn, makrothymeite pros pantas.

i18n.en: And we exhort you, brothers: admonish the disorderly, encourage the fainthearted, support the weak, be patient toward all.

notes.official: *noutheteite tous ataktous* 'admonish the disorderly': *ataktos* is 'out of order, undisciplined', used of a soldier out of rank (BDAG). The rendering 'the idle' (RSV, NRSV 'idlers') rests on 2 Thess 3:6-11, where disorder is tied to refusing to work, and on papyrus uses of the verb for absence from work (G. Milligan, *St Paul's Epistles to the Thessalonians*, 1908, additional note on *ataktos*); 'disorderly' (ASV) keeps the wider sense. *paramytheisthe tous oligopsychous* 'encourage the fainthearted' (KJV 'comfort the feebleminded'); *antechesthe tōn asthenōn* 'support the weak'; *makrothymeite pros pantas* 'be patient toward all' (ASV 'longsuffering'). 'brothers' per `adelphoi-brothers-rendering-1-thessalonians`.

paragraphs.text: ὁρᾶτε μή τις κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ τινι ἀποδῷ, ἀλλὰ πάντοτε τὸ ἀγαθὸν διώκετε εἰς ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰς πάντας.
paragraphs.translit: horate mē tis kakon anti kakou tini apodō, alla pantote to agathon diōkete eis allēlous kai eis pantas.

i18n.en: See that no one repays anyone evil for evil, but always pursue what is good toward one another and toward all.

notes.official: *horate mē tis kakon anti kakou tini apodō* 'See that no one repays anyone evil for evil' (cf. Prov 20:22; Rom 12:17; 1 Pet 3:9). *to agathon diōkete* 'pursue what is good'. Text: NA28 and the Byzantine text add *kai* before *eis allēlous* ('both toward one another and toward all'; KJV 'both among yourselves, and to all men'); the SBLGNT, Westcott-Hort and Tregelles lack it. The English is nearly the same (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).

paragraphs.text: πάντοτε χαίρετε,
paragraphs.translit: pantote chairete,

i18n.en: Rejoice always;

paragraphs.text: ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθε,
paragraphs.translit: adialeiptōs proseuchesthe,

i18n.en: pray without ceasing;

notes.official: *adialeiptōs* 'without ceasing', as of Paul's own prayer and thanksgiving at 1:2-3 and 2:13.

paragraphs.text: ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖτε· τοῦτο γὰρ θέλημα θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: en panti eucharisteite· touto gar thelēma theou en christō iēsou eis hymas.

i18n.en: in everything give thanks; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.

notes.official: *en panti* 'in everything', or 'in every circumstance'. *touto gar thelēma theou en Christō Iēsou eis hymas* 'for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you': 'this' covers the three imperatives of vv 16-18. 'God' per `theos-kyrios-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-1-thessalonians`; 'Christ' and 'Jesus' per the central `christos-māšîaḥ-anointed-one-cross-corpus-greek-hebrew-aramaic` and `iēsous-yehoshua-yhwh-saves-folk-etymology-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: τὸ πνεῦμα μὴ σβέννυτε,
paragraphs.translit: to pneuma mē sbennyte,

i18n.en: Do not quench the Spirit;

notes.official: *to pneuma mē sbennyte* 'Do not quench the Spirit': the Spirit is pictured as a fire, and the pairing with prophecy in v 20 shows that its manifestations in the assembly are meant (cf. 1:5-6; 4:8 'his Holy Spirit'). Capital 'Spirit' for God's *pneuma*, lower case for the human spirit at v 23 (`pneuma-spirit-capitalization-1-thessalonians`, following the Matthew overlay's rule).

paragraphs.text: προφητείας μὴ ἐξουθενεῖτε·
paragraphs.translit: prophēteias mē exoutheneite·

i18n.en: do not despise prophecies;

notes.official: *prophēteias* 'prophecies', the utterances of prophets in the assembly (ASV 'prophesyings').

paragraphs.text: πάντα δὲ δοκιμάζετε, τὸ καλὸν κατέχετε,
paragraphs.translit: panta de dokimazete, to kalon katechete,

i18n.en: but test all things; hold fast what is good;

notes.official: *panta de dokimazete* 'but test all things' (ASV 'prove'): *de* ties the testing to the prophecies of v 20 (cf. 1 Cor 14:29; 1 John 4:1). *to kalon katechete* 'hold fast what is good'.

paragraphs.text: ἀπὸ παντὸς εἴδους πονηροῦ ἀπέχεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: apo pantos eidous ponērou apechesthe.

i18n.en: abstain from every form of evil.

notes.official: *apo pantos eidous ponērou apechesthe* 'abstain from every form of evil': *eidos* is 'form, kind' (BDAG), not 'semblance'. The KJV 'from all appearance of evil' is a lexical choice, not a different text. *ponērou* may be a noun ('every kind of evil') or an adjective ('every evil kind', continuing the testing of v 21).

paragraphs.text: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἁγιάσαι ὑμᾶς ὁλοτελεῖς, καὶ ὁλόκληρον ὑμῶν τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ καὶ τὸ σῶμα ἀμέμπτως ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τηρηθείη.
paragraphs.translit: autos de ho theos tēs eirēnēs hagiasai hymas holoteleis, kai holoklēron hymōn to pneuma kai hē psychē kai to sōma amemptōs en tē parousia tou kyriou hēmōn iēsou christou tērētheiē.

i18n.en: And may the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, and may your spirit and soul and body be kept whole, blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

notes.official:
*Autos de ho theos tēs eirēnēs* 'And may the God of peace himself' (cf. Rom 15:33; Phil 4:9): a wish-prayer with the optatives *hagiasai* and *tērētheiē*. *holoteleis* 'completely' and *holoklēron* 'whole' stress entirety. *hymōn to pneuma kai hē psychē kai to sōma* 'your spirit and soul and body': *pneuma* is lower case for the human spirit (`pneuma-spirit-capitalization-1-thessalonians`), and *psychē* is 'soul' where it is listed with *sōma* (`psyche-soul-1-thess-5-23`). The triad occurs only here in Paul; most commentators take it as an emphatic expression of the whole person rather than a teaching that a human being has three parts (Malherbe, AB 32B, ad loc.; C. A. Wanamaker, *The Epistles to the Thessalonians*, NIGTC, 1990, ad loc.).

*amemptōs en tē parousia* 'blameless at the coming': *parousia* is 'presence, arrival', used in the Hellenistic world for the visit of a ruler or official (A. Deissmann, *Light from the Ancient East*, 1927) and by Paul for the coming of the Lord (2:19; 3:13; 4:15). 'coming' (ASV, KJV, RSV) is kept. The central `as-saa-the-hour-quranic-eschatology-cross-corpus-yom-yhwh-parousia` treats *parousia* as background to the Qur'anic 'Hour'. 'God', 'Lord' per `theos-kyrios-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-1-thessalonians`; 'Jesus' and 'Christ' per the central entries.

paragraphs.text: πιστὸς ὁ καλῶν ὑμᾶς, ὃς καὶ ποιήσει.
paragraphs.translit: pistos ho kalōn hymas, hos kai poiēsei.

i18n.en: Faithful is he who calls you, who will also do it.

notes.official: *pistos ho kalōn hymas* 'Faithful is he who calls you' (cf. 2:12; 4:7); *hos kai poiēsei* 'who will also do it', that is, will carry out the wish of v 23.

paragraphs.text: Ἀδελφοί, προσεύχεσθε περὶ ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: adelphoi, proseuchesthe peri hēmōn.

i18n.en: Brothers, pray for us.

notes.official: *Adelphoi, proseuchesthe peri hēmōn* 'Brothers, pray for us'. Text: NA28 and Westcott-Hort add *kai* 'also' ('pray also for us', as Paul prays for them, 1:2; 3:10); the SBLGNT, Tregelles and the Byzantine text lack it (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).

paragraphs.text: ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς πάντας ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.
paragraphs.translit: aspasasthe tous adelphous pantas en philēmati hagiō.

i18n.en: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.

notes.official: *en philēmati hagiō* 'with a holy kiss', the greeting of the assembly (Rom 16:16; 1 Cor 16:20; 2 Cor 13:12; 1 Pet 5:14). 'brothers' per `adelphoi-brothers-rendering-1-thessalonians`.

paragraphs.text: ἐνορκίζω ὑμᾶς τὸν κύριον ἀναγνωσθῆναι τὴν ἐπιστολὴν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: enorkizō hymas ton kyrion anagnōsthēnai tēn epistolēn pasin tois adelphois.

i18n.en: I adjure you by the Lord that this letter be read to all the brothers.

notes.official: *enorkizō hymas ton kyrion* 'I adjure you by the Lord': a formal oath, in the first person singular. *anagnōsthēnai tēn epistolēn pasin tois adelphois* 'that this letter be read to all the brothers', that is, read aloud in the assembly. Text: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read *horkizō* (KJV 'I charge you'), with the same sense, and add *hagiois* (KJV 'unto all the holy brethren') (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).

paragraphs.text: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μεθʼ ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hē charis tou kyriou hēmōn iēsou christou methʼ hymōn.

i18n.en: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

notes.official: *meth' hymōn* 'with you'. Text: the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus add *Amēn* (KJV 'Amen'); the SBLGNT and NA28 end without it (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-1-thessalonians`).
